issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Institutional Failure: The people or institutions that should have protected me let me down
issues.explanation: For a life-threatening motor vehicle collision, 'institutional failure' and especially 'betrayal by someone trusted' are hard to reconcile unless the crash involved unusual interpersonal circumstances not reflected anywhere else in the profile. The rest of the profile centers on fear/startle/intrusive sensory recall, which fits an accident trauma; these appraisal items instead imply an interpersonal or systemic-trauma narrative.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Betrayal: I was betrayed by someone I trusted
issues.explanation: 'Guilt on recall' can occur after accidents, but in this profile it sits awkwardly with the chosen appraisal set: the appraisals focus on betrayal/institutional failure rather than self-blame or responsibility. That makes the guilt theme insufficiently supported across nodes for a coherent cognitive formulation.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Betrayal: I was betrayed by someone I trusted
issues.explanation: For a life-threatening motor vehicle collision, the appraisal 'I was betrayed by someone I trusted' is hard to reconcile unless the crash specifically involved a trusted driver or intentional wrongdoing, which is not otherwise reflected anywhere else in the profile. As presented, it introduces a different interpersonal-trauma theme that is not supported by the rest of the selected items.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Self-Blame: The event happened because of the way I acted
issues.explanation: Within Negative Appraisals, 'Betrayal' and 'Self-Blame' can sometimes coexist, but in this profile they point to different causal narratives for the trauma (trusted other's betrayal vs one's own actions causing the event) without any supporting context. That makes the appraisal set clinically hard to unify around a single MVC trauma narrative.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Other-Blame Rumination: I dwell on what other people have done to me
issues.explanation: The profile contains a hard-to-reconcile blame pattern: strong self-blame and guilt are paired with other-blame rumination as a core maladaptive strategy. Mixed blame can occur, but this combination is the main internal inconsistency in the selected items because the appraisals and memory items point toward inward blame, while the strategy item points toward sustained outward blame.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Self-Blame: The event happened because of the way I acted
issues.explanation: Within the cognitive formulation, Maladaptive Strategies links most strongly to Negative Appraisals, so the strategy content should fit the appraisal style. Here the appraisal style is dominated by self-blame, helplessness, and permanent emotional damage, making other-blame rumination the least coherent strategy item.

issues.item: Memory: Guilt on Recall: When I remember the event I feel intense guilt
issues.explanation: For a life-threatening motor vehicle collision, guilt on recall is plausible, especially with self-blame, so it is not problematic by itself. The concern is specifically its combination with persistent other-blame rumination, which pulls the profile toward a different blame direction than the rest of the formulation.

vignette: Carlos Carlos is a 62-year-old Latin American man married to his lifelong partner, Rosa. He has spent most of his life dancing, an occupation that requires both physical and emotional agility. However, since the traumatic event—a life-threatening motor vehicle collision—he finds it difficult to perform on stage or even leave his home. The crash occurred one evening after a performance when Carlos was driving home in heavy rain. The roads were slick, and suddenly he heard the screech of tires followed by a deafening impact. He remembers feeling helpless as the car spun out of control, each bump and scrape echoing with the finality of impending doom. The moment his vehicle collided with another, all sound seemed to amplify into an overwhelming cacophony that has since haunted him. In the aftermath of the accident, Carlos struggles most with a sense of helplessness and character blame. He believes that the event happened because he was not careful enough and that he will never be able to feel normal emotions again. This belief feeds his heightened state of anxiety and fear. Whenever he enters any room or building now, he immediately scans for exits, reacting with alarm if anyone touches him unexpectedly. Carlos is convinced that bad things will inevitably happen to him regardless of precautions. These negative appraisals exacerbate his emotional distress, making it difficult for him to engage fully in daily activities without feeling overwhelmed by fear and shame. When he remembers the event,Carlos feels intense shame and has difficulty putting the frightening experience into words. He often hears snippets of the collision's sounds replaying in his mind, causing him to dissociate or deliberately blank out. To cope with these intrusive memories and negative emotions, Carlos tries to suppress thoughts about the trauma and stays up until very late, hoping that sleep will help him avoid the vivid flashbacks. However, this pattern only reinforces his maladaptive strategies, as it further disrupts his ability to process what happened in a healthy manner. The cycle becomes increasingly self-reinforcing: whenever he has these memories, Carlos’s maladaptive behaviors worsen, leading to even more intense feelings of helplessness and character blame. His avoidance and suppression only deepen the shame he feels when the memories surface. His occupation as a dancer adds an additional layer of complexity. Onstage, where he once moved with grace and confidence, now becomes a trigger for his fear and anxiety. The bright lights and open stage space remind him of being out of control during the collision. Carlos has begun to avoid performances and rehearsals, isolating himself from colleagues and friends who do not fully understand what he is going through. Rosa has noticed the change in Carlos’s behavior but feels powerless to help him break this cycle on her own. Recently, his reluctance to engage with others and leave their home became more pronounced, and Rosa encouraged him to seek professional help. She hopes that with support, Carlos can regain some of the joy he once found in dancing and life. Carlos is most afraid of never recovering from the trauma, losing the emotional connections with his loved ones, and being unable to return to the stage where he feels truly alive. He hopes that through therapy, he can find a way to manage his symptoms and rediscover a sense of normalcy in his life again. His journey toward healing begins as he takes the first step towards seeking help, understanding that the path ahead will require confronting painful memories and fears head-on.
